utterances.text: And no doubt, when you returned back to Holland, you saw an enormous amount of media footage in relation to the fall of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's also correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you -- perhaps, I better ask you this: What about in the debriefing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you ask him, slow down a little bit, please, between question and answer and a short pause, okay? Because we are escalating slowly. I mean surely --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'm getting a little bit excited, Your Honour. I'll calm down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: In these debriefing sessions, you've said you weren't shown any photos. What about video footage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We haven't seen video footage during the debriefing in Assen, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Nothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yet, as you've agreed, there was certainly an enormous amount of footage available just from watching the television at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And the Dutch Ministry of Defence didn't use that footage when they debriefed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's on their account if they didn't use it, so...

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. But you agree that you were in fact requested to provide information in relation to the intelligence that you gathered from your time in Srebrenica, to the Dutch Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no specific questions, as I remember, on specific intelligence matters themselves, as names, as -- if we had photos. It's quite typical because -- but I stated before, we had our own question marks at that debriefing in Assen. So you can imagine why I had those question marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So you say that was a flaw, again, in the process of debriefing, that that information wasn't provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. All right. Naturally, though, it is information that you would expect to be provided, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? All right. Now, I want to take you to your role as an intelligence officer while you were actually at Potocari. Now, I assume, Major Rutten, you're not able to speak B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B/C/S means?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Bosnian, Serbo --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No? How was it that you communicated with, in particular, the leaders of the BiH that you dealt with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly in German. The German language, they knew quite well, and we are -- Holland as -- is known about its languages as German and English as well, and sometimes French. And we can communicate quite well in that languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Did you -- you did not use interpreters at all when you were dealing with those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did use them, but not always.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. And in particular, you have identified in relation to the northern part of the enclave which was your responsibility, you've identified two particular leaders that you dealt with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes? And they were -- do you recall their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mandzic, I think, and the other one I don't know right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Sabanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Sabanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Tell me, when you met with these individuals, where did those meetings take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly in a house in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. That's the answer I'm looking for. I take it, then, that if I were to show you a map of Potocari, you would be able to mark on that map where -- you could at least try?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll try it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if 65 ter number P1522, which is an aerial of Potocari, could be shown to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, Major?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Perhaps if some assistance could be provided in terms of marking the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But on this map, the house, it was further on down the road. And it's not on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to point that out myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. I'll try another one. I've got a number here to offer the witness. Perhaps, if we could bring up P02103, photo number 6, and see if that gives you a better perspective. P02103, photo number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It's not on this photo as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you referring to a site which would be further up from the petrol station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Srebrenica. It's more -- it's in fact the situation where we are in fact village Srebrenica -- of Potocari; and here, it's marked out the compound and further down the road, the bus remise or compound. It's much higher, on higher ground to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately, I don't think we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are maps, perhaps one of the assistants could or the Prosecution could assist us there. We have seen maps that more or less show us an aerial view of the area where this site would be located. In the meantime, let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I can move on, Your Honour, and we can --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, in relays to this house that you're talking about, how would you -- was it what you considered to be a headquarters of the BiH that was being used for that purpose, or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. It was a normal house where he lived himself, Mandzic, I mean, with his wife. And his wife worked also on the compound as a laundry woman.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well, what about your knowledge of any buildings that were used in Potocari as a command for the BiH? Were you aware of that, that there was such a building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Not by my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So as far as you were concerned, they just simply had no command or headquarters in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We entered once -- we tried to enter once a house which we marked out as a form of a headquarters, but they regularly moved it to another building. So it's difficult to establish whether -- what was the actual HQ of the BiH; and, therefore, we -- and we also didn't have the authority to go into those buildings by ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- within the mandate, if you know what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But you've just indicated at least in pursuance of your role as an intelligence officer, you had made that assessment, that there was, in fact, something that was used as a kind of headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But I just explained you, it regularly moved. So you couldn't establish really where they were active at all time at the same point. So there was no reason for us to have an overview or a direct look constantly on the house, because we weren't aware of the situation that which group moved to where to or whatever. And we at that time, from April on, we hadn't enough personnel to move all those locations because, yeah, our Serb friends didn't let in our colleagues any more in the enclave who were on leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: What about your knowledge of the state of the BiH armaments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had a weapon collection point in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the Bravo compound, there were some larger material and some small arm weapons. I regularly saw that BiH soldiers were carrying weapons during my patrolling, but they --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Can I just stop you? What sort of weapons were they carrying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Small arms weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Because I just remind you of something you said at the Krstic trial. This is at page 2166, Your Honour, line 7 to 15. What you said was, "What I've seen of the BiH was that they had small armaments, partly and light mortars. That was the only thing I've ever seen by the BiH and some RPGs, that is an anti-tank weapon and that's it." That's right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That's correct? And then you went on to say, "And they had almost no ammunition," right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now I want to direct your mind to that statement. Had you, in the course of your role as an intelligence officer, specifically sought to discover what the state of the BiH's ammunition was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got the reports from the patrolling, and what we saw or what we could indicate gave us the attention that there wasn't that much ammunition, as well as our colleague in the south. And that was the Captain Groen of the Bravo Company had also given us information that there was a very poor situation on the BiH side on the ammunition, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But you just indicated yourself that it was often very difficult to make those complete assessments as to that sort of -- the state of what their ammunition was. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Difficult to know, in the same way it was difficult to know which how was being used as headquarters, because they would be changing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You also assessed these two men that you dealt with as quiet and professional. They were your words. You accept that's what you said in your Assen debriefing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Professional, I take it that your assessment was that they were professional army men in the manner in which they conducted themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The way they handled their situation, in the enclave. That was what I meant with professional. And also, professional was the way they assessed our situation, because they also -- they did the same what we did with them. They assessed our situation, and he perfectly, he, Mr. Mandzic, perfectly drew out our patrolling. And he said, "I can exactly see which patrolling is from Bravo or from Charlie Company." So he gave us a quite clear view on our situation as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You understood each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Because you then went on to say that it was easy to make effective agreements with them and contacts were smooth; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. Is it fair to say that you preferred to deal with them than dealing with your contacts on the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Because the contacts that we had on the Serbian side were more on the level of the battalion, the S5 group of the battalion with, for instance, the Major Boering.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: The liaison side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the liaison team, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Let me ask you then about your contacts with the Serbian officer that you did, who did you have contact with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only ones that I have contact with were the ones that is I met near OP Papa.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Right. That was, what, near Yellow Bridge, around that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That's it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And was that limited contact that you had with --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very limited.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. I want to take you to the 13th of July, Major, and the sequence of events on that day. Now, you've already been cross-examined quite extensively about your movements on that day, and I don't propose to take you through exactly what you did all day. But I do want you to start with -- you were the duty officer on that morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, being the duty officer entails being in the operations room; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, being in the operations room of the Charlie Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And that normally entails being there all day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not all day. A few hours, and then there is a the next one is coming up.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. So when did you start that morning being duty officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Can you give me a time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 7.00, 8.00. Must have been 7.00 or 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: How long did that last for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's difficult, yeah, in the -- until a few hours later in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Then what your evidence has been is that the next thing you do is go to the "White House," is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Can you give me a time that you first went to the "White House" on this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Must have been sometime before noon, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Can you -- you've already indicated in your evidence that you went inside the house that day. This is on the first occasion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Did you take photos on this first occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No photos on the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Right. That you spoke to some of the Dutch soldiers that were outside on the first occasion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? How long would you say that you spent at the "White House" on this first time on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only give you an estimation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three-quarters of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. What was the next thing that you did after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went towards the APC blockade, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. That -- and who did you speak to at the blockade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Can you indicate who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a few NCOs, they were in my previous platoons, spoke about it. They were on the APCs and had various talks with colleagues. So it's difficult to indicate every thing that --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Is that where you heard the rumour in relation to the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? If -- just reminding you of something that you said in the parliamentary inquiry, that you said it was about noon that you heard the rumour in relation to the dead bodies, does that sound correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that sounds correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: As you've already given evidence you then went on foot the to the place where the bodies were alleged to be; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: How long did it take you to arrive at that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: How long were you actually at the location where you found the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five minutes or more.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhat -- it's difficult to say now. It's a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you then returned once back to the compound, back to the operations room; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We stayed on the -- we went through the blockade as we came back, and I spoke to the Lieutenant Colonel Karremans on the road. And I didn't went directly back, but later on I went back and to inform my company commander as well what I've seen during my visit to that meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. I want to ask you about your report to Colonel Karremans about this. What you said was he gave a half hearted response; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you yourself had some fairly negative views in relation to your battalion commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? You described him as a -- as dictatorial in his leadership style; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You perceived him to be a remote figure, when I say that there was a complaint that he only visited the OPs I think once and he did it in one day, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: He was responsible for thoughtless comments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Were those thoughtless comments in relation to what was going on in the ground around Potocari on those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But also what happened earlier. My colleagues were looking for a sense of leadership, and we were missing that sense of leadership. And this is the thing, you could say, about the Lieutenant Colonel Karremans.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: What about Major Franken? Was it fair to say that the day to day leadership was in his hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's fair to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Now, just in relation to going back to Colonel Karremans, you have a specific recollection of seeing him on the 13th of July, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you saw him with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you say that they were having a conversation at the entrance of the compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, again, I'm going to test your powers of memory, but can you give me a time frame as to when you say this conversation was occurring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later in the afternoon, but I -- it's very difficult to say now.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this? Was it before or after you had been to the "White House" for a second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: It was after?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. We'll get to your movements later in that day. So what you say about this conversation between General Mladic and Colonel Karremans is that you gleaned from the topic of the conversation that it was in relation to an inspection of the compound that night; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And as far as you're aware, did that inspection occur on the night of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was an inspection of the compound.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And that was an inspection by General Mladic, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He wasn't on the compound himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It were other Serbian colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And that was an inspection that was carried out with those Serbian colleagues and Colonel Karremans, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Not with Karremans, with the Major Franken.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now, we digressed a little about your views of the leadership of the battalion. Once you had made the complaint to Colonel Karremans, you then made another complaint to your company commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And then you went to the blocking positions again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. And this is the time at which you had the conflict with Lieutenant van Duijn; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Again, can you give me some indication of what time that was that the conflict with Lieutenant van Duijn occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also in that afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. And I don't want to labour this conflict that you had with him. But it's fair to say, isn't it, that you left the scene, because of the extent of the disagreement that you had with him, with Colonel Creemer, I think it is, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You left with him, I mean with Colonel Creemer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you returned to the compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Not directly. All right. Where did you go after you left -- after you'd had the conflict with van Duijn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed on the road somewhat further down the line towards the entrance of the compound , and I talked with the Colonel Creemer about the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Did he have to calm -- he had to calm you down a little bit, is that fair. I'm not being facetious saying you got emotional. I'm just saying, as I understand it, you had to be calmed down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I doubt that, but okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: At what point did you then go back to the "White House?" This is for a second time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After I went on the compound, because I had a driver with a jeep being ready at the compound to escort the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now your driver's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Verbugt.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Verbugt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Verbugt. It's a difficult language, I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. And again, I do want to take you through the detail of your movements at the "White House" on the second occasion. And I'm reading from your summary, your evidence in Krstic. Okay? But what you said is you said to your driver, as you were waiting for the last buses to leave, "It's good to get some witnesses. You come with me to the "White House." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So just you and him went on your own at that stage; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived there, you saw the two Dutch soldiers that had been stationed outside there, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Did you see -- was there -- Major De Haan, was he there as well at this stage on the second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No? And what you've indicated is, first of all, you walked around the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So you walked around the perimeter of the house, that's the first thing you did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: With him, with your driver?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. Then you say that you went to the side that was empty that same morning. Okay, which side of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you're standing in front of the house, the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. You say there were two Bosnian Serb soldiers on the staircase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: When you say staircase, is if the house was in fact open, so you could see the staircase inside; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was partly open.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. Then you say the staircase was filled up with Muslim men, and you say the moment you came around the corner of the house. Now, can you describe that a bit for me, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you're standing in front of the house, it's at the left-hand side; and if you're walking along the front side of the house, then you get on your right-hand side the corner, and then you see the staircase as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. And then you have a specific recollection of Bosnian Serb soldiers with money and deutschmarks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you say they stopped doing that when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. Then you say you walked around the house, I presume you then go to the front of the of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went at the back side first.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But then well you've gone on to say in the front of the house, there was a balcony that was filled up with refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So I presume you're at the front of the house at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And you observed that it was completely filled up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now, from that first moment of walking to the house with your driver, and that point when you're at the front of the house, what period of time -- again, I'm going to have to be as -- I appreciate it's difficult, but just give me an estimate. How long did that process take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Did you speak to anybody at that -- during that process, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spoke to the two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: The Dutch soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who were telling me about transferring the deutschmarks, so I tried to have a look at myself whether that happened or not. I tried -- yeah, I spoke some -- I think two Serb soldiers shortly.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But you're not entirely sure about that recollection, is that -- right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But the problem is a lot of people around and it's happening -- a lot of things at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You have a lot on your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Of course. So what you then say is you went back to the entrance of the compound; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. So that's, as we know from the photo, that's across the road from the "White House." And you spoke to Rave and a Dutch Major to try and get the men out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I -- did you, after going back to the entrance of the compound and speaking to Rave, did you at any stage go back to the "White House?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No? You're in -- you're sure about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to clarify two things with you, Major. The first is - and you were cross-examined about this quite extensively last week by my learned friend Mr. Ostojic - and you were asked about that portion of your statement, this is 3D37, at page 4, where you were asked about that assertion that you had gone to one of the Serbian leaders and told him that he ought to arrange something for the evacuation of the Muslim men. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. And when you were cross-examined by -- on it by my learned friend. You accepted that that was in fact what had happened. You had gone to a Serbian leader to speak to him that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you to 3D41, at page 18, and if you can -- this is your -- this is the statement that you gave to the Kodak team. And, well, perhaps to be fair to you in terms of context, if -- if we can begin on page 17. Thank you, Madam Usher. You'll see there is a reference there to the paragraph that begins,"The Dutch soldiers present asked whether we ought to talk to someone about the transport for these men." Can you see that, at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes? And then, if we go to the next page, please, at the top. So page 18, it says -- you see that there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: "We arranged for transport by buses together with Sergeant Major Raven of intelligence." Now, can you clarify for me, please, which is correct? Did you arrange for the transport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No? So that's incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's incorrect. We, as stated last week also, "we" means Rave and De Haan. We spoke about it, as mentioned, and the situation was that we asked, in fact, or I did, the UNMOs to try to contact the Serbs to do something about the situation. And last week I, as I recall it, I said that the situation was that we weren't in control but, in fact, the Serbs were. So the moment that we tried to ask for it, the buses were already on the way because it happened shortly afterwards. So that was the reason that I, last week, rose that question that I said, "Yeah." In fact, we were asking it, but it was already planned that the house would be emptied by the -- by the way, at the same time as I said. Yeah. It happened almost in the same move that -- yeah, in the same sequence as we had that talk about, "Look the house is overfilled, what's going to happen there," and so on and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Just so I understand your answer, what you say is that it was simultaneous; that you in fact were in the process of arranging for transport and it had already happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were -- we weren't able to arrange anything because, we were asking. And we were saying, "You have a situation with a lot of people. What you going to do about that?" And if I say we arranged for transport, then it's more we had the idea to try to arrange transport but we weren't in control, so we weren't able to arrange anything. We just were asking, "Is it possible that you can ease the situation by having the men out of the house?" Because it was totally filled up.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. So just so I understand what's written in your statement to the Kodak team, while it appears to indicate past tense, that you'd arranged for transport, that's not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's semantic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: It's a matter of semantics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's a word thing. I must say that, because last week happened the same thing. You're trying to give a situation where everything happens in minutes and time frames, and giving the whole situation a totally different view then. And that is something that doesn't happen in the real life situation. You aren't walking around with your eyes on your wrist; How long have I been here? How long am I travelling from right to left? So yes, I getting a little bit irritated, I know, but that's no real operational situation. I'm sorry, I must say that because that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I don't mean to irritate you, Major. I'm just asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm just saying how does -- how this kind of text gets interpreted and then we get a different situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I want to ask you about what I just clarified that there were only two occasions that you went to the "White House" on the 13th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Perhaps if I could get you, please, to have a look at 3D37, page 4. This is your statement to the ICTY. Do you have that there in front of you? And I think it's the next page. It's not my page -- yeah, the next page, sorry, my mistake. All right. Now, if you can just focus your mind on that paragraph where it says, "I walked back with van Schaik to the house." This is the second time that you arrive at the "White House," is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Van Schaik was also the first time around when I was with the"White House".

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can focus your mind in this way, you're recounting a visit to the "White House" after the discovery of the nine bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. So if we look at it like that, then it's fair to say, is it not that this is the second time you'd been to the "White House?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. So you say that you walked back with van Schaik. Now, at this stage, you don't indicate anything about walking there with your driver. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And then you recount what we've been through already, that you observed that the house was full?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes? And then you also indicate that Major De Haan was in fact at the "White House" on this occasion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? So, again, your memory perhaps is failing you a little bit before when you said he wasn't there on the second occasion? I'm not criticising you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. But the second time the situation we spoke about was the situation at the opposite of the house with Sergeant Major Rave around and there was Major De Haan. The time that I saw him with the house, yeah, could have been at the same movement. Yes, could have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So your memory now was he was in fact there on the second occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, could have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Now you then go on in the next paragraph to say, "I then went to see my company commander." So you've left the "White House" obviously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, then, you go on in the paragraph that begins, "I then walked back to the house with Private Verbugt." You see that there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So, in fact, it appears from the way I read it, and please correct me if I'm wrong, that there were three occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, could have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Again, difficulty with your memory, because there was a lot going on in your mind on this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But now you're over 11 years, there have been a lot of statements, you're putting now for different years, statements next to each other and pick out words where there is one, two, three, or four times that I've been at the house. There was a visit that I stayed somewhat longer, if it's 15 or five minutes. Okay, then I've been three times -- I was three times there. It could have been. It's difficult to say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Can I put this to you? This third occasion that you speak of in your statement, you say that you approached the house and all you saw was the BSA soldiers taking money. That was an extremely quick visit on that final occasion, you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The visit with Verbugt was, as I told you before, only 15 minutes. Rather than connect the persons with the visit, then we have the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to ask you some questions about -- well, actually before I do that, can I ask you this? You've made some -- you've had some grievances about the debriefing statements as not being an accurate representation of events from your perspective. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I assume that you don't have the same complaint when it comes to this statement taken in October 1995 by the ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you can -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Can I say that? You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I want to ask you just briefly about the fate of the film that failed to materialise. You know what I'm talking -- in relation to the photos you took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, can I ask you this. Many how many rolls of film had you taken when you left -- when you left the former Yugoslavia on the 21st of July, I think it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ones I had on me, two.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You had two. Now, tell me, were they both rolls of film that reflected the events that had been going on in and around Potocari on these days that we are talking about, the 12th, the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And you made a decision not to hand over that film while you were in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You didn't trust -- there was a question of trust as far as you were concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And then when you were back in Holland, you indicated to the Ministry of Defence that you would hand this material over, for obvious reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, was it the 23rd or the 24th of July that you handed that film over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came back on Monday, and on Tuesday I handed the film over.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And that was done in, is it fair to say, fairly informal circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It's fair to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Because you were visited at your home by I think it was Mr. de Ruiter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Major de Ruiter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Who was he? Was he present in Sarajevo during this period or is that a different --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. But he was from the Ministry of Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: From the intelligence department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And you told him what was on both of these rolls of films; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. He was only asking me for one film and that was the film where I photographed the --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: The bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bodies, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. So, well, you've clarified that for me, then. So in fact, you only handed over one roll of film to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. You're correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And that was a roll of film that you were told over the phone the next day had been destroyed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. Did you ever at any stage receive any official written report as to the fate of the film or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Never?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Later on there were reports, but not on the fate of the film itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Because I'm interested in a comment that you made in your Assen debriefing. This is 3D44, at page 2. Do you have that there in front of you, Major?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? You'll see there is a comment that you make where you refer to the photo roll available to Major de Ruiter, and then you go on to say still has some photographic material and you're willing to make that available. So this is at the 6th of September 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: What -- well, I'll ask you this: When you refer to the photographic material there, is that the second roll of film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. And you indicate that you're willing to make this available if some indication could be given of what is being looked for. I'm particularly interested in that statement by you. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. As I said it there, what are you looking for, I can then explain what is already -- because I -- at that time, the second roll was developed. And I could tell them what there was on the second roll. So I could explain to them what there was on the roll, if they asked me the question what they were looking for.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But we've established, have we not, that what was on this second roll were photos that you took as to the events in and around Potocari on these days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So am I to take it from that that there were photos of a similar nature in terms of photos of what was going on at the blocking positions with the separation or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A part of those photos have been shown in the Krstic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That was my next question. So these photos that you have, you have given to the investigators of the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the Krstic case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And can you tell me how many photos there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven or eight that I were -- that were in relation to the happenings on the 12th and the 13th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. I want to ask you about, in fact, my next topic is some evidence that you gave in the Krstic trial. You'll recall that in the course of giving evidence in that trial, and in this, you were shown a photo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And what the Prosecutor said to you in the Krstic trial was that you had seen that photo before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? I want to ask you about that, and I appreciate that this is really going to test your memory. But no doubt, prior to you giving evidence in the Krstic trial, you were subject to a proofing session by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. In the same way you were here a number of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was once here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: We will get to the number of proofing sessions you've had for this trial in a moment. But I want to ask you about your proofing session prior to giving evidence in the Krstic trial. You recall the name of the Prosecutor in the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Tell me, who was present at this proofing session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Just the two of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Can you tell me how long that went for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only thing is a day, I think, it was on a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So actually you seem to -- you can recall the actual day, so you have a reasonable memory of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Because it's a typical day to still work on a Sunday here, yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So it went all day, and it was just the two of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, this might seem like a very obvious question. But no doubt, while you were being proofed by him, he took notes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. And given that it went for a day, he was no doubt taking notes for the entire time that you were going through your statement, yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Now, no doubt the beginning of the proofing session -- perhaps I'll ask you: Do you have any specific recollection of how that proofing session began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spoke about the situation on the different kinds of statements that there were already here in the ICTY, yeah, by the Office of the Prosecutor, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And no doubt you read your statements thoroughly in the course of that proofing session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, there were less statements on the table than now -- than there are now.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But the statements that you did have in front of you, then you read thoroughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And as we've established in the course of this proofing session, you were shown a photo by Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Something else happened. I told him that I was sent again on a mission abroad. It was in the course of the conversation. And I said that I will be going to Banja Luka again in two or three months. And he said, "Oh, that is interesting," and then he called a colleague. And I didn't exactly know what he was weighs talking about. He said, "Can I show you some video?" And we saw some video, and there were some persons on it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'll just stop you there. At what point in the proofing session did this occur? Was it in the middle? Was it towards the beginning? Was it at the end?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon somewhere, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And the context in which his suggestion -- well, perhaps I'll establish this first. Obviously, it's his suggestion to show you a video, you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. And can I ask you this? Was it related in any way in the context of your -- of a discussion about your role as an intelligence officer while you were at a time Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. The question was put more, put like, I said I was interested in pictures of persons that I had seen, probably had seen, during those days. And he said during the day, "Later on I can show you some video. Perhaps you'll recognise someone."

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. So just so that I understand exactly, so that you, in fact, said you were interested in pictures of persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because he --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this, just before you answer, was that in response to him already indicating that he had some videos that he wanted to show you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. No. We were talking about -- as I said before, about my mission abroad. And I asked him where the persons that you going to show? Are they still in Serbia? Where are they at the moment? We talked about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And in response to that specific inquiry of yours as to whether or not people were still in Serbia, he then said, "Well, I've got a video that you maybe interested in watching?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. He suggested that there were some material that he would later on show me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. But in that regard, it's fair to say, isn't it, that when you watched that video. The seed had been planted in your mind, so to speak, that there were going to be persons on that video that you might be interested in, in relation to the investigation? That's fair, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The first pictures that I saw, I didn't recognise any of them at all. So, yes, there wasn't planted nothing, I think, but okay, not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No, but Major Rutten, you appreciate this was part of an investigation -- an investigative process, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: It was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You agree with that, yes. And so when Mr. Harmon says to you, "I have some video material that you may be interested in," you know, in your mind, what the purpose is behind showing that to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but the purpose of being around that day was also very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that question was asked and he provided an answer. And it's being asked again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree 100 percent with you. There could have been no other purpose for showing him this video, Ms. Condon.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll just -- I just want to take you up on your last question, Major -- sorry, your last answer. Was that what you said was, I just want to get the sequence right, "The first pictures that I saw, I didn't recognise any of them at all." All right? So when you say the first pictures that you saw, so that I understand the sequence, are you referring to the first video that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It were video pictures that were freezed more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. So we know we need to establish this. So, in fact, what you were shown first was a stills from a video; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell me how many you were shown?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: It was in a book form, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It were some pictures, stills, as you call it, from videos, and I don't recall how much I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No. No, sorry. It's my fault because my question wasn't clear enough. I would like to know what form they were shown to you in. It was a situation where there was, "Here have a look at there photo," then the next, or was it a book where you were asked to flip through the book and say, "Do you recognise any of these people?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was stills from a video picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: On a computer screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On a screen, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And what you've indicated is that from the -- the first time, there was no recognition at all of anybody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Nothing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just the situation I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But not the persons who were on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No, no. But I'm obviously focusing our mind on a particular process where you say, "Oh, I recognise that person." Okay? That's what I'm asking you about. So what then happened? You said, "Well I don't know recognise anybody here." Were you then shown a video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I only saw freezed video images.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. And then, what, you looked at them again and then you say you had -- you recognised somebody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Then we saw other pictures. And there, I recognised someone.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Right. And again, can I ask you, the other pictures that you saw, how -- in what sequence? Was it ten pictures that were offered to you? Was it 20? Was it 30? Was it 50? How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Many. But, yeah, there were many shown, yes. Many stills on the video. I don't know how much, but a lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Can I ask you how long that process took, or you don't have any recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Sometime. It can be 15 until 30 minutes I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: See, what I -- apparently, what you told -- I'm not trying to trick you, but I just want to clarify this. In your proofing -- well, I'll ask you this now: How many proofing sessions have you had with Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Just one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One and -- one in an evening before I came here on last Tuesday, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And the first one was on the 9th of November, I think, from memory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And tell me this: Were you shown any videos or photos in that first proofing session?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. And in the second proofing session last week, you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. And he asked you, Mr. Thayer asked you, what had happened at the Krstic proofing session, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And you told him that Mark showed you a video in which you recognised some people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And also a book of photographs in which you recognised some people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Is that correct? Let me ask you this: When you say you recognised the people on the video, they were different to the persons that you identified in the stills; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes in not the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. A lot of them, not now. One -- one was and a lot of them, I didn't see before.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Can you help me out here a little bit? I presume that you weren't shown the video last Tuesday night with Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I haven't seen the video, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well, from your memory, tell me how long does that video last for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The session with Mr. Harmon, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I don't know. I don't know. I saw only the stills of the video, and I saw not the complete video.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So in effect, just -- you didn't see a compilation of images when you refer to it as a video; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was stills from a video. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you saw those images, this is in your proofing session with Mr. Harmon, those stills, were they images that were familiar to you from media reports of the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Had you seen any of those images before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No? They were completely new? Some of them familiar at least?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They were new to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now, you would agree, wouldn't you, that -- and I certainly -- if you need to have a look at your statement again, then I can bring it up for you. But there is simply no reference at all in your October 1999 statement to having seen a person outside the "White House" who you refer to as not a plain soldier. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. That there stand again no description, nothing, about this person in your October 1999 statement, yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And, obviously, obvious question, but you've already been asked it. Your memory in relation to the events is going to be far more accurate in October 1995 than it is in April of 2000, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But that questions were never asked in previous statements before 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So there are a lot of questions that weren't asked in Holland in the various interviews that I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But we've already established insofar as your ICTY statement is concerned, the October 1999 -- 1995 one, you don't have any complaints or grievances as to the completeness of that statement? Sorry, is that funny?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is funny. Because when you're sitting there for a number of time, and they don't ask you questions that you by yourself don't see as a question, is there -- and if later on there comes another one and asks specifically about other things, then you answer that questions at that time and not, oh, you haven't asked me that question on that particular time. It wasn't the case, it wasn't the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So what you say is the fact that that's not contained in your statement is simply down to the fact that you weren't asked the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that you also had the wherewithal to include in that statement reference to a specific Serbian leader that you went to speak to about events in the "White House." You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and they never asked me about the identity of the person. They never asked for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. But you agree that in your proofing session last Tuesday night with Mr. Thayer, you were asked to recall what uniform this man was wearing at the time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. And on Tuesday evening, your answer was, "I cannot recall." You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That's in the proofing note, I can show you. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And now, in your evidence in this trial last Thursday, in response to the same question, you say, "He was wearing camouflage trouser and a green-brown T-shirt."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because that was the answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Hold on. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? Now, that's because you'd seen the photo, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. So, in fact, it's fair to say, is it not, that without you being shown this photo, Major Rutten, you have no independent memory of this person that you say you saw outside the "White House." You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. He may not have an independent memory the way you've been putting it on what he might have been wearing. Doesn't necessarily translate into not having an independent memory of the face of that person, for example, or the stature of that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Perhaps Your Honour. If I follow up with an if you more questions on this point and I am about to move to another topic. And I see the time as well. It's nearly time to break.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Again, I just want to remind you that in your October 1995 statement, there is no reference to the actions of this individual at all, in any way, shape or form, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am about to move to another topic and I see the time. And I appreciate that this cross-examination will be divided, so perhaps if I could seek the Court's indulgence and conclude here for the day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Major, did you have an opportunity to discuss with the VW unit about your availability?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They haven't spoke to me until this moment, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When do you think you can return for conclusion of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I Haven't my agenda here with me, so certainly not this week because I have a completely booked agenda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to have it postponed beyond the 14th of December. So if you could find a day when you could return before the 14th of December, when we go on recess, after which we go on recess. Perhaps you can communicate it now the Victims and Witnesses Unit or maybe even the registrar will communicate with you and give you the various options, contact numbers, et cetera and then you need to let us know and we can accommodate you. In the meantime you need to make some adjustments, but I don't think we should leave a long interval of time between now and when he will testify again.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just to appease Major Rutten, I suspect I have another hour of cross-examination and then I'll conclude with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But then we have another two teams so that may amount to another hour so we are talking of a whole session at least, or more than a session, yeah. So you will need to make adjustments. The moment he communicates to us the possible dates, we will see what options there are, Major, and we'll try to adjust our schedule accordingly. And in the meantime, again, once you are still testifying, please do not communicate with the Prosecution or anybody else for that matter, and then you will return when -- on a day when it will be convenient for you. Okay. I think you can be escorted now out of the courtroom. Thank you, Major --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- for your patience and cooperation. And we'll meet again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Tomorrow, we are starting with the new witness, 70. I'm just confirming orally that this witness will testify with the following protective measures: That's facial distortion and pseudonym. All right. I take it the position with the Defence is precisely that, no objections, in relation to the next one. And if you could let us have your objections or your points in writing at the earliest possible we will try to come down with our position by tomorrow or Wednesday at the latest. The earlier you feed us your position on these protective measures, the earlier we will come back to you. Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, just to alert you. I think the main argument will be on Serb witnesses regarding protective measures, is my understanding, and the -- also, we will be in touch about the next witness because if the next witness comes back like we all hope next week, that may change our whole witness arrangement in terms of these witnesses. So we'll be in touch as we get our schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You know you can take it for granted that we interfere the least possible, if at all, with scheduling of -- but I think it's desirable not to delay the continuation of this witness's cross-examination beyond what is reasonable when our memories would still be fresh. Okay. Thank you. Tomorrow it's sitting in the afternoon. We will need to make an adjustment in the timing. We'll need a break at 5.30 because we have a Judges' meeting at 5.30 which will last about half an hour. So it will not be the usual -- there will be the first break at the usual time but then we'll need to break again at 5.30 so make the necessary arrangements. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
